answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains that climb like a vine across verified tasks, validated via zero-knowledge proofs. Minting clustered identities imposes superlinear staking fees: each duplicate identity doubles bonding requirements, turning a minor fee into an impassable financial canyon. Staked collateral docks on an on-chain jetty, ensuring exponential capital exhaustion collapses coordinated swarms.
